body:
## Summary

The shared read/repair validation paths accept decoded fragments based on `chunk_id`, but do not verify that the fragment header matches the requested `FragmentId.index` or expected EC scheme tuple.

## Evidence

Observed during adversarial review against the assurance map:

- `crates/core/src/repair.rs`: `fragment_intact` and `intact_shard` validate `decoded.header.chunk_id == chunk` only.
- `crates/core/src/read.rs`: the Reed-Solomon read path fetches a requested index, decodes bytes, checks only `chunk_id`, then pushes the payload under the requested index.
- `crates/custodian/src/reconstruction.rs`: reconstruction uses `repair::intact_shard` and associates the returned shard with the requested index.
- `crates/custodian/src/scrub.rs` and `crates/custodian/src/rebalance.rs`: maintenance paths use the same shared helper.

`FsChunkStore::verify` currently checks both chunk and index, so the issue is partly masked for the current filesystem-backed path. The assurance boundary is still too low: future backends, object-store adapters, or adversarial/corrupted backend responses could return a valid same-chunk shard for the wrong index.

## Impact

A same-chunk/wrong-index shard can be accepted by shared core/custodian code and then fed into reconstruction as if it belonged to the requested index. That can produce wrong reconstruction input, hide placement corruption, or weaken the `never wrong bytes` assurance if the backend does not independently enforce the full fragment identity.

This relates to the assurance-map open items around M4.6/adversarial validation and future storage/topology surfaces.

## Suggested fix

- Change shared validation helpers to accept the expected `FragmentId` and expected `EcScheme`.
- Verify at least:
  - `decoded.header.chunk_id == expected.chunk`
  - `decoded.header.ec_fragment_index == expected.index`
  - for RS fragments, header `ec_k`/`ec_m`/scheme type match the committed `ChunkRef.scheme`
- Add regression tests with a test store that returns bytes for the same chunk but the wrong `ec_fragment_index`.

title: Validate fragment index and EC tuple when accepting stored fragments
